items.title: Live: Herzog welcomed at Government House as peaceful protesters gather outside Parliament
items.description: Israeli President Isaac Herzog is welcomed to Canberra as protesters gather on the lawns outside Parliament House. Follow live.

items.title: Woman kills nine in mass shooting at school, house in Canada
items.description: The shooter was a woman, described in an official active shooter alert put out in British Columbia described the suspect as a female with brown hair, who was wearing a dress.

items.title: Liberals plot mass resignations, paving way for leadership challenge
items.description: Liberals are bracing for a wave of frontbench resignations as soon as Wednesday to pave the way for Angus Taylor to mount a leadership challenge against Sussan Ley.

items.title: Person detained in relation to Nancy Guthrie disappearance
items.description: Law officials in Arizona say a person has been detained for questioning in relation to the disappearance of Nancy Guthrie, the 84-year-old mother of Today show host Savannah.

items.title: Children at 'imminent' kidnapping risk by man who built secret loft in his home
items.description: WA Police say "something terrible" could have happened if there was a delay in intercepting a Baldivis man who planned to abduct and sexually abuse a child in Perth.

items.title: The only Olympic sport that doesn't let women compete starts tonight
items.description: Nordic Combined is the only sport at any Olympic Games — summer and winter — that does not have an event for women. It's an omission that is putting the entire future of the sport at risk.

items.title: 'How dare you': The 29-year career behind this former cop's viral DV lecture
items.description: Years on the front line of domestic violence surfaced in a frustration-filled moment on national television for Vincent Hurley. He explains what motivates him to keep fighting for change.

items.title: Two more Chinese nationals charged with foreign interference
items.description: A man and woman have been charged under foreign interference laws after a task force began investigating the covert collection of information about a Canberra Buddhist association last year.

items.title: Top cop raises concerns about sentences for people who assault officers
items.description: South Australia's police chief is seeking further advice from the Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) after a woman who had assaulted a police officer with a glass bottle was spared jail.

items.title: No body-camera footage of woman's death in police stand-off, coroner hears
items.description: A court hears a NSW inquest will need to rely on eyewitness accounts of the 2023 death of Krista Kach, who was shot with a beanbag round following a 10-hour stand-off with police in 2023.

items.title: As Epstein spotlight shifts to UK, Trump could have 3 million reasons to worry
items.description: Donald Trump's enemies made no secret of their hopes the documents would contain something explosive enough to bring the president down, but right now the Epstein spotlight is on Britain's politicians and palaces.

items.title: Here's what's really causing millions of mortgage borrowers grief
items.description: It may sound boring, but "capacity constraints" are to blame for your higher mortgage repayments.

items.title: Live: ASX 200 rallies as CBA surges, Aussie dollar above 71 US cents
items.description: The Australian share market is higher on the first "big day" of reporting season with good news for Commonwealth Bank, but CSL shares are down sharply a day after the biotech giant dumped its chief executive, Paul McKenzie. Follow live.

items.title: What's better than a Muppet Show revival? One with Sabrina Carpenter
items.description: Kermit, Miss Piggy and the rest of the crew are back to celebrate their 50th birthday with a one-off special that has the potential to turn into a whole new series for the beloved characters.

items.title: New engines, no DRS and other important changes to Formula 1 in 2026
items.description: New engines, new regulations and an 11-team grid are just some of the changes in Formula 1 this season. Get up to speed with what is new in F1 ahead of the Australian Grand Prix.

items.title: Emergency warning issued for grassfire north of Melbourne
items.description: Residents near Sunbury, north of Melbourne, are advised to shelter now as a grassfire burns out of control.

items.title: Travel quiz: Which Spanish city hosts a tomato-throwing festival?
items.description: Which European country has no McDonalds? And where's Australia's most western point?

items.title: Victorian government defends action on construction sector amid CFMEU allegations
items.description: The Victorian government is defending its handling of corruption in the state's construction sector amid accusations in a major corruption report that it was "cowed" by the CFMEU.

items.title: Missing man separated from friend while collecting firewood, police say
items.description: A 32-year-old man missing in Tasmania's north was collecting firewood with a friend when the pair became separated on Sunday, police have said.

items.title: Major change could be coming to supermarket shelves
items.description: The nation's food ministers will this week take a crucial step towards mandating the Health Star Rating scheme on packaged food products.

items.title: Next fight looms after Qld government loses appeal in battle for sacred springs
items.description: Wangan and Jagalingou peoples await the state government's next move after a win in their fight to have alleged damage to a sacred site near a mine in Central Queensland investigated.

items.title: Indonesia to send up to 8,000 troops to Gaza under Trump's Board of Peace
items.description: The move makes Indonesia the first country to clearly commit troops to a multinational peacekeeping effort in the war-torn enclave.

items.title: Woman 'frustrated and mystified' after Uber guide dog case settles
items.description: Uber quietly agrees to an external review of its Australian operations after settling a Federal Court case brought by a woman refused more than 30 rides while travelling with a guide dog.

items.title: CBA shares up after bank reports increased profits
items.description: CBA's net profit for the first half of the financial year rose 5 per cent to $5.367 billion, beating analyst expectations, on the back of increased lending and deposit volumes.

items.title: Farmers lay blame for devastating fires at WA government's feet
items.description: Farmers and volunteer firefighters say decades of neglect by WA's Department of Biodiversity, Conservation and Attractions is at the heart of fires that ripped through more than 200,000 hectares of state-managed land.
